en.title: Holiday food and gifts
en.summary: What people eat and give at Christmas and other festivals.

paragraphs: Food and gifts are a central part of festivals. This lesson describes traditional meals and gives you practice with the present continuous for plans and the present perfect with yet.

The traditional Christmas dinner in Britain and America is roast turkey with potatoes, vegetables and gravy, followed by Christmas pudding or pie. Presents are exchanged on Christmas morning, and children hang up stockings on Christmas Eve. A family in Bath is getting ready for the day.

lines.speaker: Dad
lines.text: I am. And Grandma is bringing the Christmas pudding.

lines.speaker: Mum
lines.text: Have you wrapped all the presents?

lines.speaker: Dad
lines.text: Not yet. I'll do it this evening.

lines.speaker: Mum
lines.text: And the turkey? Has it come out of the freezer?

lines.speaker: Dad
lines.text: Yes, I took it out yesterday. It needs five hours in the oven.

lines.speaker: Mum
lines.text: We should put it in at eight.

lines.speaker: Dad
lines.text: The children are going to be up at six, so we'll all be awake anyway.

paragraphs: **1. The present continuous for arrangements.** Use am, is or are + -ing, with a time word, for plans that are already fixed. See Introduction to Grammar: Future and other tenses.

blocks.html:
FormExample
is bringingGrandma is bringing the pudding.
am makingI am making the gravy.
are comingThe cousins are coming at noon.
aren't workingWe aren't working on Boxing Day.

paragraphs: **2. Not yet and already with the present perfect.** Not yet shows something still to do; already shows it is done. See Introduction to Grammar: Past tenses.

blocks.html:
FormExample
haven't + participle + yetI haven't wrapped them yet.
have you + participle + yet?Have you wrapped them yet?
have already + participleI've already bought the cards.
has just + participleShe has just left.

items: Turkey is the traditional Christmas meat in Britain and America.
Mince pies are small fruit pastries eaten in December.
A Christmas cracker is a paper tube that pops open and contains a paper hat and a small joke.
Boxing Day is the day after Christmas, 26 December.

paragraphs: In the United States, the biggest family meal is often Thanksgiving, also with turkey, and Christmas is celebrated with presents and a large meal. Gifts are given to children and adults alike, and cards are posted weeks in advance.
